stem: A nurse enters a room, adjusts an IV pump in the patient's immediate surroundings without touching the patient, and then leaves. When is hand hygiene indicated?

options.A: Hand hygiene is not required because the nurse did not touch the patient directly.
options.B: Perform hand hygiene after touching equipment in the patient's immediate surroundings, even without direct patient contact.
options.C: Perform hand hygiene after equipment contact only if the device is visibly soiled.
options.D: Defer hand hygiene until the next patient-care task because no blood or body-fluid exposure occurred.

rationale: CDC healthcare hand-hygiene guidance lists hand hygiene after touching a patient or the patient's surroundings as a clinical indication. CDC Isolation Precautions specifically includes contact with inanimate objects, including medical equipment, in the immediate vicinity of the patient. Therefore, direct patient contact, visible soiling, or blood/body-fluid exposure is not required for this hand-hygiene indication.
educational_objective: Perform hand hygiene after contact with equipment or other surfaces in a patient's immediate surroundings, even when the patient was not touched directly.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Clinical Safety: Hand Hygiene for Healthcare Workers
source_locator: Recommendations → 'Know when to clean your hands' → 'After touching a patient or patient's surroundings'; supporting Isolation Precautions recommendation IV.A.3.e for inanimate objects/medical equipment in the immediate vicinity.
source_claim_supported: CDC explicitly identifies hand hygiene after touching patient surroundings and after contact with inanimate objects including medical equipment in the patient's immediate vicinity.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Appendix A, printed p. 26, Safety and Infection Prevention and Control → Standard Precautions/Transmission-Based Precautions/Surgical Asepsis: apply infection-prevention principles including hand hygiene.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — hand hygiene

source_original.stem: A nurse enters a room, adjusts an IV pump in the patient’s immediate surroundings without touching the patient, and then leaves. When is hand hygiene indicated?

options.A: Hand hygiene is not required after leaving because the nurse did not touch the patient directly.
options.B: Hand hygiene is indicated after touching equipment in the patient’s immediate surroundings, even without direct patient contact.
options.C: Hand hygiene is needed after equipment contact when the device is visibly soiled, but routine contact alone does not create an indication.
options.D: Hand hygiene can be deferred until the next patient-care task because no body-fluid exposure occurred.

source_original.rationale: CDC hand-hygiene guidance includes performing hand hygiene after touching a patient’s immediate surroundings or equipment, even when the patient was not directly touched.
source_original.source_detail: Indications for hand hygiene, including after touching patient surroundings/equipment. Current CDC hand-hygiene guidance at cited URL; rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control; Reporting of Incident/Event and infection/safety activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the construct and key. Tightened the rationale and distractors to the exact CDC indication after contact with patient surroundings/nearby medical equipment; no extra method, duration, or visibly-soiled requirement was introduced.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Hand hygiene after contact with patient surroundings
audit_findings.source_authority: Official CDC hand-hygiene and Isolation Precautions guidance.
audit_findings.currentness: CDC Clinical Safety page dated February 27, 2024 and rechecked 2026-08-16.
audit_findings.exact_locator: 'Know when to clean your hands' and Isolation Precautions IV.A.3.e directly support the scenario.
audit_findings.claim_audit: No unsupported requirement for visible soil or body-fluid exposure remains.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because direct patient contact is not required.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because visible soil is not a prerequisite for this indication.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because hand hygiene is indicated after the surroundings contact, not deferred.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B matches the stated clinical indication.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address timing/indication for hand hygiene; no numerical or unrelated cue.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Confirmed that the answer does not over-specify sanitizer versus soap-and-water, which depends on additional conditions not present in the stem.
